facts.text: Writer-director Zachary Will got the idea for Grandma Werewolf at a Thanksgiving dinner in his parents' cabin. Then he shot the movie there, and his parents let the crew use it for free.
The idea began as a joke at a Thanksgiving dinner: someone noted a missing grandmother couldn't fly away like a vampire, and director Zachary Will suggested she might be a werewolf.
Grandma Werewolf was director Zachary Will's first feature. Before it, he had made about 50 short films and worked on reality TV episodes.
One night shoot at Blue Mountain Ski Resort in Pennsylvania was a car chase in which Grandma Werewolf actress Tricia Harmon attacks the crew's car. The Times News visited that Saturday night.
Local Pennsylvania businesses and property owners donated locations, including Blue Mountain Ski Resort, which producer Olivia Dean said took a lot of the financial burden off the production.
When rain threatened, the crew moved a car scene indoors. They shot it in a garage against a green screen instead.
The cast and crew came together from Georgia, New York, Michigan and elsewhere to shoot in Carbon and Monroe counties, Pennsylvania, chosen for their scenery.
Shooting spread across Kresgeville, Palmerton, Jim Thorpe and Kunkletown, Pennsylvania. Sunny's gas station in Kunkletown was one stop on the schedule.
Director Zachary Will grew up in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, studied film at Full Sail University and later worked in Atlanta before making this film back in Pennsylvania.
Film Threat's Bobby LePire described the werewolf mask worn by Tricia Harmon as cheap latex. He added that the flat direction and sparse sets make it the most eye-catching thing on screen.
Rafael Malaret was the film's editor and post-production supervisor. He described his job as making sure everything looks real on a very small budget.
Director Zachary Will's own filmmaker profile lists corporate videos made for PepsiCo among his 50-plus short projects, and a feature documentary, Business Not as Usual, came after this film.
Film Threat's Bobby LePire gave Grandma Werewolf 2 out of 10 full moons. He said the actors playing the siblings feel like real siblings and have fun together.
Film Threat called the film's 90-minute runtime punishing. Yet Rotten Tomatoes lists about 73 minutes and Apple TV lists 1 hour 12 minutes, so streaming cuts seem to differ.
Film Threat's Bobby LePire called the two cop characters delightful scene-stealers. They are played by Chris Naples (Jared) and a costar, and they got a mock monster-hunting ad after the credits.
Wayne Shearer plays The Master, a magician who teaches spells. Film Threat's Bobby LePire said Thomas Sigurdsson's hunter character was played fine but was pointless.
Film Threat's Bobby LePire compared the film unfavorably to ThanksKilling, saying that movie succeeds by leaning on gore and jokes instead of hiding its low production values.
Writer-director Zachary Will volunteered at his high school library, and that library shows up in some of the film's scenes.
Stephanie Malone of Morbidly Beautiful called it a campy, low-budget B-movie with heart. She said it never plays Grandma's grief as melodrama and compared it to a big side dish of Mac and Cheesy.
Stephanie Malone of Morbidly Beautiful praised Tricia Harmon's physical comedy as Grandma. Her 2023 review ran in the site's Tubi Tuesday series, where the film was streaming free.
Tricia Harmon plays Grandma. Film Threat's Bobby LePire called her sweet in the role, and the film was still being finished for a Thanksgiving 2017 target release.
The film's Thanksgiving release target was set while it was still shooting in summer 2017. Filming was in its last weeks by the end of July 2017, with post-production to follow.
Star James Wosochlo (Hank Malroy) later appeared in the crime thriller 21 Bridges, Creed II and The Many Saints of Newark, according to his IMDb credits.
Wosochlo's Hank was singled out by Film Threat's Bobby LePire as truly terrible. LePire liked the siblings, though: Trevor Brooks (Ben) and America Ramos (Kate) feel like real brother and sister.
